slides.headline: She was born in Mumbai, trained as an engineer. In 2026, she became dean of a top US nursing school.
Dr. Kavita Radhakrishnan became permanent Dean of UT Austin's School of Nursing on September 1, 2026
slides.body: Mumbai-born, she earned her bachelor's in electronics engineering from the University of Mumbai before moving to the US, later earning a PhD in Nursing Science and joining UT Austin's faculty in 2012.

slides.headline: She holds over $10 million in NIH and federal research funding, focused on digital health for chronic disease management.
slides.body: In 2025, she was inducted into the Sigma Theta Tau International Nurse Researcher Hall of Fame - and much of her research specifically targets culturally-tailored health interventions for South Asian communities.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when an engineering degree from Mumbai becomes the foundation for leading American healthcare research.
slides.body: Radhakrishnan's path - engineering to nursing science to dean - is a reminder that Indian STEM training opens doors far beyond the field someone first trained in.
